_comment: Inference-side sweep for the released v2 checkpoint. No retraining, no code changes --
only flags evaluate_full.py already accepts, so nothing here can regress the model.
What is being tested:
halo      context ring (m) around each scored chunk. Wider = more context for boundary
voxels. Only cores are scored, so coverage never changes.
core_max  scored voxels per chunk. Larger = fewer chunk boundaries = fewer seams.
Constraint: core + halo points must fit in --block_size (20480). Raising core_max eats
the halo budget, which is why the two are swept one at a time around the current values
rather than as a full cross product.
Stage plan (screen cheap, confirm expensive):
noise        baseline x3 at tta_d4 1 -- establishes how much a difference must beat
screen_halo  halo sweep at tta_d4 1
screen_core  core_max sweep at tta_d4 1
confirm      best 3 overall, re-run at tta_d4 8 x2 -- the protocol the record uses
Run:  python sweep_eval.py --config sweep_eval.json
python sweep_eval.py --config sweep_eval.json --dry_run
FOLLOW-UP (added after the first pass). The first pass showed the real variable is not
halo width but the halo BUDGET: chunk_with_halo() keeps only block_size - core_max halo
points and randomly discards the rest, so widening halo at a fixed core_max just spreads
the same budget thinner. mIoU was monotonic in the budget:
core_max 8192 confirmed at 8 views: 65.01 vs the 64.79 record, twice, spread 0.00.
So: push the budget further, and re-test halo width now that there is room to retain it.
